posts.caption:
Lesson 1 of the ABAP course: the Data Dictionary (DDIC).

Every table, structure, domain and data element your programs use is defined centrally in SE11.

1. One transaction for tables, views, types, domains, search helps and lock objects
2. Saving creates an inactive version only
3. Activation generates the runtime object (nametab) that programs read

slides.title: A full *ALV report* in 5 lines
slides.voiceover: A full ALV report in five lines? No field catalog needed.
slides.spoken: A full ALV report in five lines? No field catalog needed.

slides.heading: *CL_SALV_TABLE*
slides.code:
cl_salv_table=>factory(
  IMPORTING r_salv_table = DATA(lo_alv)
  CHANGING  t_table      = lt_orders ).
lo_alv->get_functions( )->set_all( ).
lo_alv->display( ).
slides.voiceover: Call the SALV factory, pass your table, switch on the toolbar, and display.
slides.spoken: Call the SALV factory, pass your table, switch on the toolbar, and display.

slides.label: RECAP
slides.heading: *factory* then *display*
slides.body: Columns come from the table type automatically.
slides.voiceover: The columns are built automatically. Save this.
slides.spoken: The columns are built automatically. Save this.

posts.caption:
Still building a field catalog for every simple report?

CL_SALV_TABLE gives you a full ALV in a few lines:
1. factory( ) with your internal table
2. get_functions( )->set_all( ) for sort, filter and Excel export
3. display( )

Columns and headings come from the table type. Wrap the call in TRY...CATCH cx_salv_msg.

Which ALV do you use most: SALV or REUSE_ALV_GRID_DISPLAY?

slides.title: Inside a *domain*: the Definition tab
slides.voiceover: A domain is more than a data type. Let's look inside SE11.
slides.spoken: A domain is more than a data type. Let's look inside SE11.

slides.heading: Definition *tab*
slides.voiceover: Data type, length, output length. And the most important field, the conversion routine.
slides.spoken: Data type, length, output length. And the most important field, the conversion routine.

slides.heading: *ALPHA* adds the leading zeros
slides.code:
lv_order = '1234'.
CALL FUNCTION 'CONVERSION_EXIT_ALPHA_INPUT'
  EXPORTING input  = lv_order
  IMPORTING output = lv_order.
" lv_order = '0000001234'
slides.voiceover: The screen shows 1234, the database stores it with leading zeros. To convert in code, call ALPHA INPUT.
slides.spoken: The screen shows 1234, the database stores it with leading zeros. To convert in code, call ALPHA INPUT.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: One domain, *many fields*
slides.body: Every data element on this domain gets the same type, length and conversion.
slides.voiceover: One domain, many fields. Change the domain, and they all change.
slides.spoken: One domain, many fields. Change the domain, and they all change.

posts.caption:
Domains, Part 1 of 3: the Definition tab in SE11.

A domain defines the technical attributes that every data element built on it inherits:
1. Data type and number of characters
2. Decimal places and output length
3. Conversion routine, e.g. ALPHA, which stores 1234 as 0000001234
4. Lowercase flag
